q: Is the cross-subsidy surcharge on open access capped at 20% of the average cost of supply?
title: Surcharge cap at 20% of cost of supply
short: Yes. Rule 13 of the Electricity Rules, 2005, added by the Electricity (Amendment) Rules, 2022 on 29 December 2022, says the surcharge a state commission fixes for consumers seeking open access shall not exceed 20% of the average cost of supply. Your state tariff order applies it.
audience: Open access consumers and factories checking their landed power cost

p: Rule 13, Surcharge payable by consumers seeking open access: the surcharge determined by the State Commission under section 86(1)(a) of the Electricity Act, 2003 shall not exceed twenty per cent of the average cost of supply.

sections.h: How it interacts with the green rules
ul: Under the Green Energy Open Access Rules, 2022, the cross-subsidy surcharge for a green open access consumer may not rise by more than 50% over the level fixed for the year open access is granted, for twelve years from the renewable plant's commissioning.
No cross-subsidy surcharge or additional surcharge applies when green power is used to make green hydrogen or green ammonia, or when it comes from a non-fossil waste-to-energy plant.
Captive users who pass the captive tests do not pay the cross-subsidy surcharge.

p: Find the average cost of supply in your commission's latest tariff order and multiply by 0.20. If the cross-subsidy surcharge in your open access invoice or offer is higher, ask the discom which order it is applying.

example.title: Worked example: checking the cap (illustrative figures)
lines: Average cost of supply in the tariff order: ₹7.20 per kWh
A cross-subsidy surcharge of ₹1.80 per kWh in an offer would be above the cap; ask which order it comes from
